tasks.short: Decide a meeting is needed, then invite buyers and sellers.

steps.what: List the open details that still need the two parties.

loop.output: Open detail and who must answer it
loop.check: Drop a detail with no note
loop.why_not_simpler: A note can hide that the point is already agreed

steps.what: Decide a meeting is warranted before any invite goes out.
Propose times only after that meeting decision.
Confirm a time they can attend.
Arrange meetings between buyers and sellers on negotiated details.

tasks.design: Open details are listed from the deal notes. The agent decides a meeting is warranted, and only then do invites go out. The seller confirms a time. The agent arranges the meeting and sits in it. Negotiating the points is this meeting, not a separate chase of calendars.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings were proposed because a party asked, even when the open point was a missing document.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar slots can be proposed. Deciding the meeting is deserved cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing which detail will actually move if the parties sit down.
tasks.human_edge: The agent cancels a meeting that would only repeat a point already agreed.

ambition.what: Each proposed meeting is marked warranted or not, against a named open detail.

tasks.altitude: The meeting stays. The agent can refuse to invite people when the detail does not need them in a room.

reach.task: Plan a day around meetings that already have a reason
reach.learn: Which meetings are fixed enough to plan around

evidence.claim: A calendar can propose times. Deciding that a negotiation needs a meeting stays with the agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from deal notes to a held meeting on named details. The seller's confirmation is the seller's time.
Fields: open detail, who must answer, proposed slots. Fallback: no invite.
Use the {CALENDAR} the office already has. Upkeep of 2 hours covers the detail headings.
This task is arranging the meeting. It is not the longer negotiation that happens across many calls.
If the parties have no shared calendar, the proposal fails and the agent phones. That case is the low end.
unknowns: Whether both parties already share a calendar.
Who usually refuses the first time.
research_questions: What share of proposed meetings does the agent later cancel as unnecessary?

incremental.description: Keep the detail headings the meeting decision uses

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: calendars do not match and every meeting is still arranged by phone, so little shrinks. High: invites go out from a decision, the seller's confirmation is not saved, and the meeting stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draft the lease, negotiate it, and send only the accepted version.

steps.what: Fill lease drafts for the properties the clients named.

loop.output: Lease draft of the standard clauses
loop.check: A blank stays blank rather than being guessed
loop.why_not_simpler: Standard clauses do not hold this tenancy

steps.what: Read lease clauses the standard template does not hold.
Show the properties and negotiate the lease on the clients behalf.
Accept or refuse the tenant in person, with no score.
Send the lease version the agent has accepted.
File the signed lease on the clients record.

tasks.design: A lease draft fills standard fields from the property and the parties. The agent reads the clauses the template does not hold, shows the property, and negotiates. Accepting a tenant is a human decision with no score. Only that version is sent for signature.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leases were copied from the last file, including clauses that did not fit, and tenant choices were informal.
tasks.enabler_now: Names, rent and dates can fill a standard draft. Choosing a tenant cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing a clause that looks standard and is not, for this building or this tenant.
tasks.human_edge: The agent refuses a tenant, or a clause, and says why to the client.

ambition.what: Each applicant is marked accept, refuse or need-more, by the agent, before a lease is sent.

tasks.altitude: Viewings and negotiation stay. The agent can refuse to send a lease, and can refuse to use a score.

reach.task: Set the clauses an agent may not change alone
reach.learn: Which lease terms the broker treats as fixed

evidence.claim: Standard lease fields can be filled from the records. Choosing a tenant and reading unusual clauses stay with the agent.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from a property and a client to a filed lease. A purchase-agreement filler is not used here. The lease template is the office's own.
Fields: parties, property, rent, dates, and the standard clauses. The agent produces the tenant decision. Fallback: leave a clause blank.
Configure the template in {DOCS} before a new drafter. Upkeep of 4 hours covers clauses.
Whether a national reading of the high-risk rules treats tenant selection as high-risk is unknown. This design does not score applicants.
unknowns: Whether tenant selection is treated as high-risk under a national reading.
research_questions: What share of lease drafts need a clause the template does not hold?

incremental.description: Revise standard clauses when the office changes its lease

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the tenancy is unusual, so the draft is rewritten and the negotiation stays. High: standard fields fill, the viewing and the tenant decision stay, and no score is used.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit and assess the property before it is shown to a client.

steps.what: Visit the properties and assess them before any showing.
Turn the visit notes into a defect and access list.

loop.check: Drop a line the notes do not support
loop.why_not_simpler: A quick note misses the thing that will bother a buyer

steps.what: Decide if the properties are fit to show to clients.
Write the note the next showing will rely on.

tasks.design: The visit happens first. Notes become a defect and access list, and the agent decides whether the property is fit to show. The showing note records that decision. Nothing is sent to a client in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Homes were shown on the first visit, and the agent discovered the problem with the client standing there.
tasks.enabler_now: Notes can become a list. The decision to show is still the agent's.
tasks.still_hard: Judging a smell, a stair or a neighbour that will matter to this client and not to a form.
tasks.human_edge: The agent holds a property back.

ambition.what: Each property is marked show or hold before a client is invited.

tasks.altitude: The visit stays the bulk of the week for this task. The agent can hold a property that the list made look ready.

reach.task: Leave a property out of a day's visits
reach.learn: Which holds are firm enough to plan around

evidence.claim: Visit notes can be listed. Assessing a property before a client sees it stays with the agent on site.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from an unvisited property to a show-or-hold note. The later showing is a different task.
Fields: defect, access constraint, show or hold. Fallback: hold, if the notes are too thin.
Upkeep of 2 hours covers list headings. The class is human.
No client message is sent here, so there is no separate approval.
unknowns: Whether sellers expect the agent to visit alone first.
How often a hold is overturned.
research_questions: What share of properties are held back after the assessment visit?

incremental.description: Keep the access headings the show-or-hold note uses

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the visit is the task and the notes stay messy. High: the list and the note shrink a little, and the visit stays at full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Submit a standard hookup form and phone the utility about exceptions.

steps.what: Prepare service hookups details from the clients property.

loop.check: Leave a field blank when the record has no value
loop.why_not_simpler: Flats hide which meter belongs to which door

steps.what: Check the form before it goes to the utility companies.
Submit the approved hookup form to the utility portal.
Connect the service or return an exception.
Contact utility companies when the portal rejects the hookup.

tasks.design: The form is filled from the address and the move date, checked, and submitted on the utility's portal. The utility connects the service. When the portal rejects the form, the agent contacts the company by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every hookup was a phone call, even the ones that were only a name and a date.
tasks.enabler_now: A standard form can be submitted. A meter that does not match the door cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Finding the right meter, or the right company, when the portal says no.
tasks.human_edge: The agent knows when to stop resubmitting and call.

ambition.what: No new service. Standard hookups are submitted, exceptions are still called.

tasks.altitude: Exception calls stay. The agent can refuse to submit a form with a blank address.

reach.task: Say which hookup failures the office escalates
reach.learn: Which rejections should be phoned the same day

evidence.claim: A standard utility form can be filled and submitted. Exceptions still take a phone call.

assumptions: Focal role is the sales agent. Boundary: from an address and a move date to a submission or a phone call. The utility's connection work is supplier time and is not saved.
Fields: address, move date, utility type. The client produces the move date. Fallback: blank field, do not submit.
Use the utility's portal. Upkeep of 2 hours covers form fields.
The class is human where the portal rejects the form. Those calls remain.
unknowns: Which utilities offer a portal an agent can use.
How often a meter number is missing.
research_questions: What share of hookups are rejected and become a phone call?

incremental.description: Update form fields when a utility changes its portal

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most hookups are exceptions and stay as phone calls. High: standard forms are submitted, the utility's connection time is not saved, and rejections are still phoned. The gross figure looks high because supplier time sits outside the agent's baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The negotiation meeting, the lease conversation, the assessment visit and the awkward utility call stay. Invites, drafts and standard forms are prepared and can be withheld.
reach: Travel agents: plan around meetings and showings that are already confirmed or held
skills_to_grow: Cancelling a meeting that has no open detail
Reading a lease clause the template does not hold
Knowing when a portal rejection needs a phone call
role.ambitious_version: A meeting is invited only after the agent says it is needed, and a lease goes out only as the version the agent accepted.
